Hey all, just want to flag something early.

We’re currently taking on more than our capacity allows. We don’t have the bandwidth to support everything coming our way, so we need to be very deliberate about what we commit to and the level of quality we can realistically deliver.

There’s a lot that needs to get done, but the reality is we’re not equipped to handle all of it at once. If we keep stretching, we risk spreading ourselves too thin and not doing justice to any of it.

I’d suggest we *prioritize hard*, align on what actually moves the needle in the short term, and treat everything else as *best-effort* rather than something we’re held strictly accountable to deliver against.

`<http://Customer.IO|Customer.IO> update`

I spoke w customer service today - here's a breakdown:


*Privacy, Security & Data Protection*

Here are the key resources for your legal team:

1. *Security overview:*<https://customer.io/security>
2. *Detailed security practices:*<https://customer.io/legal/security>
3. *GDPR compliance:*<https://customer.io/legal/gdpr>
4. *Privacy policy:*<https://customer.io/legal/privacy-policy>
5. *Data Processing Addendum (DPA):*<https://customer.io/legal/dpa/> — your legal team can download our signed agreement and send it to <mailto:gdpr@customer.io|gdpr@customer.io>
6. *Security certifications:*<https://docs.customer.io/accounts-and-workspaces/security-certifications/>
A few highlights your legal team will likely want to know:

<http://Customer.io|Customer.io> is *SOC 2 Type II certified* (Security & Availability) and *ISO 27001 certified*
We're *HIPAA-ready* with Business Associate Agreements available if needed
We're fully *GDPR compliant*, with support for data rectification, right to be forgotten (via our suppression feature), and a comprehensive audit trail
All data is encrypted in transit with TLS, and you choose whether your data is stored in our *US or EU data center*
• You control what PII you upload to us. We act as a *data processor* for your customer data, and we encourage masking or limiting any sensitive data that isn't necessary for your messaging
If your legal team needs to review our SOC 2 report, it's available at <https://my.pima.app/p/customer-io>. For questions about our Data Protection Officer, they can reach out to <mailto:dpo@customer.io|dpo@customer.io>.

*Regarding your privacy policy:* You'll want to update your privacy policy to disclose that you share customer data with <http://Customer.io|Customer.io> as a service provider/data processor. The specifics depend on your jurisdiction and existing policy language, but our DPA can help frame that relationship for your legal team.

*Opt-Out & Unsubscribe Management*

<http://Customer.io|Customer.io> gives you flexible tools to manage user preferences across email and push:

1. 1. *Global unsubscribe:* Setting a person's `unsubscribed` attribute to `true` stops all email, SMS, and push messages to that person. You can set this via our API, SDK, or through the built-in unsubscribe links in your emails. More here: <https://docs.customer.io/journeys/unsubscribes/>

2. 2. *Subscription center (recommended for your use case):* This lets you create topic-based preferences so users can opt out of specific message types while staying subscribed to others. For example, a user could opt out of marketing push notifications but keep receiving email updates. More here: <https://docs.customer.io/journeys/subscription-center/>

3. 3. *Push-specific opt-outs:*

If a user turns off notifications in their *device settings*, they simply won't receive push from your app at the OS level. No action needed on your side.
For *in-app opt-out toggles*, you can use our SDK or API to set the `unsubscribed` attribute or update their subscription topic preferences, depending on how granular you want the control to be.
Our SDK's `clearIdentify()` method disassociates a device token when a user logs out, so push notifications won't be sent to that device anymore. More here: <https://docs.customer.io/journeys/device-tokens/>
4. 4. *Right to be forgotten:* If a user requests full data deletion, you can suppress their profile in <http://Customer.io|Customer.io>, which prevents all future data collection and messaging. More here: <https://docs.customer.io/integrations/getting-started/data-compliance/>

For the best experience, I'd recommend setting up the *subscription center* with topics for your different message channels (email, push, etc.). This gives your users clear control while keeping you compliant.

I know this is a lot of info! But please let us know if you have any other questions or if there's anything else we can help with!

I think we might be mixing two different things here - the desired notification experience vs what our current system can actually support.

What Mike outlined makes sense directionally, no disagreement there. But just to level set - the framework we’ve been building towards (<http://Customer.io|Customer.io> + current backend) doesn’t support that level of granularity today.

The model outlined here requires a more robust backend + eventing + data pipeline than what we have right now. It’s a separate layer we’d need to *design* and *build*.

So I want to align on timing vs ambition.

Short term:
• Basic marketing notifications (push/email) for new user onboarding - realtime
• Retention / engagement blasts -> daily (driven by nightly batch updates of content/signals)
• Generic deep links (e.g. open app / go to feed), not highly personalized destinations
Longer term:
• Fully personalized notifications (digest, topics, creators, streaks, etc.)
• Requires proper tracking, segmentation, and triggering infra
• Deferred deep links
